answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate a rolling window of verified task-completion timestamps before it gains influence; idle or bursty participation decays its weight. Sybils must sustain real work across many sessions, so cloning identities multiplies the constant per-identity attention cost — compute, latency, and opportunity lost on other tasks — without proportional return. Growth is thus gated by verified history, not instant payment. Timber, echo, and whisper events in the ledger each require distinct proof;
